prompt: Build the debug view of a prepared statement: count the real ? placeholders and substitute the bound values, quoting and escaping correctly. Complete both methods.
explanation: A placeholder is only a placeholder outside a quoted literal, so both methods scan character by character with an inLiteral flag rather than using indexOf or split. Values are rendered the way SQL expects them: numbers and booleans bare, NULL as a keyword, and everything else single-quoted with each embedded quote doubled -- the same escaping a driver applies. Rejecting a mismatched parameter count catches the single most common prepared-statement bug before it reaches the database.
hints: One boolean, flipped every time you see a single quote, is enough to know whether you are inside a literal -- two quotes in a row flip it twice and end up back inside, which is exactly right.
Write a small helper that turns one value into its SQL text: null becomes NULL, a Number or Boolean becomes value.toString(), everything else gets quoted.
value.toString().replace("'", "''") does the escaping; check the parameter count BEFORE you start building the output so the exception comes first.
